extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, librarians, and prospective authors seeking information about the Annals of Mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article describing the Annals of Mathematics journal: its history, publication details, indexing, open-access policy, and impact metrics. Useful for readers wanting bibliographic and background information about this specific journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists the journal's discipline simply as 'Mathematics', indicating its subject area and target scholarly field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal's language of publication is English (as stated in the infobox).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states the journal is published every two months (i.e., bimonthly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher / Institutional affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Published by Princeton University and the Institute for Advanced Study (United States)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal is jointly published by Princeton University and the Institute for Advanced Study; these institutions are relevant for authors, readers, and library subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes the journal has 'Delayed' open access: articles are not freely available until 5 years after publication. It also records that an electronic edition was available without charge until 2008 and that issues from before 2003 were transferred to the JSTOR archive (non-free).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact factor and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact factor 5.7 (2023); ranks third out of 330 journals in the category 'Mathematics'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bibliometric indicator (from Journal Citation Reports) is presented as a measure of citation impact and relative standing among mathematics journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracting and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracted and indexed in the Science Citation Index, Current Contents/Physical, Chemical & Earth Sciences, and Scopus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing of major abstracting/indexing services that include the journal; relevant for discoverability and library cataloging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard abbreviations and identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard abbreviations (ISO 4: Ann. Math.; MathSciNet: Ann. of Math.) and identifiers (CODEN ANMAAH; ISSN 0003-486X; JSTOR 0003486X; LCCN 49006640; OCLC no. 01481391).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliographic abbreviations and codes for citation, indexing, and library systems are provided in the infobox.

rubrics_metrics.name: History and editorial heritage
rubrics_metrics.description: Established in 1874 (originally The Analyst); continued from March 1884 as Annals of Mathematics; notable editors include Solomon Lefschetz (1928–1958).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The historical narrative explains origins, editorial moves (Des Moines → Harvard → Princeton), key editorial periods (Lefschetz), and statements about the journal setting high standards for American mathematicians (quote from Norman Steenrod). This contextualizes reputation and editorial influence.
